correctness.rationale: An invariant barycentric point has equal coefficients across whole edge orbits. A cross-cycle edge orbit is a matching exactly when cycle lengths coincide, with d phase shifts for each equal-length pair; an intra-cycle matching orbit occurs only for even d via antipodes. Compatible orbits occupy disjoint ground cycles, proving the exact PL join B_{d,m} and factor face polynomial. For even d, the singleton-toggle poset-fiber matching is acyclic by the cluster lemma; unmatched faces are exactly perfect labeled pairs, giving contractibility for odd m and a wedge of d^(m/2)*m!/(2^(m/2)(m/2)!) spheres of dimension m/2-1 for even m; joins produce the final all-even type. The argument handles empty-face join units and m=1,2. An independent ground-edge-orbit enumerator verified nine mixed parity/cycle type cases, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The older involution-specific result is expressly a special case, and published Singh and Mondal–Mukherjee–Saha matching-complex work treats nonequivariant matching complexes and higher matchings. Bate–Everitt–Ford–Ramos calculates homology representations of other matching complexes, not geometric cyclic subgroup fixed sets. The exact all-cycle-length fixed PL model and all-even wedge formulas were not implied by inspected theorems. This is a best-of-knowledge claim, not certified priority.

value.rationale: The exact geometric fixed space for every permutation cycle type is a structural equivariant invariant. The closed integral sphere-wedge formula provides a natural family and explicit component counts that cannot be deduced from ordinary Betti numbers or from isolated involution cases. It distinguishes geometric fixed realization from fixed-vertex subcomplex, important in equivariant topology.
